segments.title: Opening and Roger Mitchell's address near the San Jacinto site
segments.summary: Tape begins on 19 January 1972 with confirmation of Mitchell's address, a block from where San Jacinto Hall stood.

segments.title: The San Jacinto headstone and the club's presidents
segments.summary: Mitchell wishes he had saved the founders' headstone; he names presidents Warren Edwards and Monette, who lost the club's money, and Benzie (Edmund Fourier), who bought it.

segments.title: Apartments, gym and Sunday boxing at San Jacinto
segments.summary: After Benzie bought the club Mitchell rented out rooms and ran a gym upstairs with Sunday boxing; Harold lists fighters who trained there.

segments.title: Layout of the hall and club banquets
segments.summary: Dance hall downstairs, members' offices and card room upstairs; Mitchell fixed a lounge, and clubs held banquets there.

segments.title: Bands and dances at San Jacinto, Frank Pena and Mitchell's own ball
segments.summary: Harold names bands that played the big hall (Don Albert, Sam Morgan, Celestin, Buddy Petit, Tuxedo); Frank Pena of the Dewdrop sponsored dances, and Mitchell ran his own ball in the 1940s.

segments.title: San Jacinto badges, later presidents and Mitchell as treasurer
segments.summary: Members wore metal badges and got into dances free; after Monette, Webber took over and Mitchell was treasurer.

segments.title: Harold's cousin Johnny Brunious and Harold's family
segments.summary: Harold talks about his first cousin Johnny Brunious (Slack Loon Johnny), a New York trip in 1936, and his mother's Planchard family.

segments.title: Tremé Market and the curfew bell
segments.summary: Recollections of Tremé Market, the bell on the neutral ground rung at nine o'clock for the kids, and relatives nearby.

segments.title: Neighborhood demolition and Dr. Coco
segments.summary: Brief talk on blocks being torn down, then Mitchell on his friend Dr. Coco and an old photograph of his family.

segments.title: Claiborne Williams' big band at the dances
segments.summary: Harold recalls dances in 1929 where the Donaldsonville band of Claiborne Williams, with son George, was hired.

segments.title: The Lions Club parade and its live lion
segments.summary: Social and pleasure club parades, including the Lions Club parading a real lion.

segments.title: Night parades and the old brass bands
segments.summary: Night parades with brass bands such as Celestin's and Keppard's.

segments.title: Flambeaux torch carriers and paper lanterns
segments.summary: Harold describes beautiful paper flambeaux carried so musicians could read music at night parades, compared to today's oil cans.

segments.title: Carnival floats and hobgoblins; why night parades ended
segments.summary: Mule-drawn floats, the hobgoblins from uptown, costumes, and how parades changed.

segments.title: Watching parades from Maison Blanche
segments.summary: Mitchell worked at Maison Blanche and watched parades from the 13th floor.

segments.title: Monday banquets and picnics of the social clubs
segments.summary: Clubs held Monday banquets at Economy Hall with bands like Punch Miller or Chris Kelly; people ate and enjoyed themselves, and Mitchell says there were no bad people then.

segments.chapter: Safe streets, decline and club life at San Jacinto
segments.title: Safe streets in the 1930s and walking home from gigs
segments.summary: Harold and Mitchell contrast safe nights then with today, recalling walking home with a horn and cheap sandwiches.

segments.chapter: Safe streets, decline and club life at San Jacinto
segments.title: Why San Jacinto declined, and cheap prices then
segments.summary: The club declined after the money was mismanaged and members died; prices in the 1930s were very low.

segments.chapter: Safe streets, decline and club life at San Jacinto
segments.title: Card games, pool and the radio parlor at San Jacinto
segments.summary: San Jacinto offered cards, pool tables and a parlor with a radio for members.

segments.chapter: Safe streets, decline and club life at San Jacinto
segments.title: Prize fights at San Jacinto and young Polite
segments.summary: Sunday fights; fighter Young Polite and trainer Albert Greger, and how Polite left for California.

segments.chapter: Safe streets, decline and club life at San Jacinto
segments.title: Herb Morand, Lizzie Miles and a photograph
segments.summary: Harold mentions trumpeter Moran and his step-sister Lizzie Miles, and says he has an original photograph of her.

segments.chapter: Safe streets, decline and club life at San Jacinto
segments.title: Neighborhood life and Mitchell as scout leader
segments.summary: Harold on the neighborhood where everyone belonged to clubs; Mitchell on his Boy Scouts group and how children's respect has faded.

segments.title: Founding date of San Jacinto and its name board
segments.summary: No record survives since the cornerstone was destroyed; Larry Bornstein got the name sign; the club predates World War I and had a junior division.

segments.title: Joining a club: references, black ball vote and meetings
segments.summary: Members came from all over; new members needed a recommendation and a black ball or white ball vote; meetings were twice a month.

segments.title: Back yard of the hall, Mitchell living there, members' trades
segments.summary: The club bought land through to the next street; Mitchell lived upstairs and downstairs; most members were skilled tradesmen.

segments.title: Multiple memberships and the Bulls Club dances
segments.summary: People belonged to several clubs; the Bulls Club hosted bands and public dances, and Harold rehearsed there on Tuesday nights.

segments.title: Knights of Peter Claver, secret societies and the Masons
segments.summary: Mitchell's Catholic order versus social and pleasure clubs, with wake guards and comparison to Masons' degrees.

segments.title: Other clubs Mitchell belonged to
segments.summary: Mitchell founded the Good Timers; Harold played picnics for them; Po' Boys and Jolly Boys.

segments.title: Artesian and Economy Hall societies and their banquets
segments.summary: How benevolent societies at Artesian and Economy Halls gave banquets, with banquet funds from the treasury.

segments.title: Urban renewal and overpasses
segments.summary: Talk on the demolition for the culture center and overpasses, then Harold says Mitchell needs his rest.

segments.title: Mitchell's birth date and birthplace
segments.summary: Born 8 August 1897 in Tremé, lived in the neighborhood all his life.

segments.title: Mrs. Balkans of Jackson Brewery and the Bo Bromo club
segments.summary: A woman salesman for Jackson Brewery, her husband's club and his illness.

segments.title: Mitchell's Knights of Peter Claver certificate and lost pin
segments.summary: Harold reads Mitchell's Fourth Degree certificate; Mitchell lost his merit pin and had a stroke in his hand.

segments.title: Wrapping up the tape and how Harold found Mitchell
segments.summary: Closing remarks and thanks; Harold says Chester Jones directed him to Mitchell's house.

segments.title: Mitchell's birthplace on St. Philip and the 1913 storm
segments.summary: Born at a two-story house at St. Philip and Prieur; Harold remembers the September storm and the lost iron bridge.

segments.title: Photographs of Mitchell and his wife
segments.summary: Mitchell shows colored wedding photographs.

segments.title: Archive at Tulane and changes in the city
segments.summary: The tape goes to the Jazz Archive at Tulane; Mitchell recalls pedaling a wagon through muddy streets.

segments.title: Model T days and closing
segments.summary: Harold and Mitchell recall Model Ts, plans to find a picture, and the tape runs out.
